name: Quanta Services
year: 1997 roll-up (IPO 1998), per company history; not re-verified this run
acquisitions: Serial acquirer since formation; 2025 deals include Dynamic Systems (per Q2 2025 release)
evidence: FY2025 revenue +20% to $28.48B, record adj. EBITDA $2.88B, total backlog $43.98B, FCF $1.67B
lesson: The roll-up model works at scale, but even the category leader earns ~10% adj. EBITDA. Scale buys craft-labor depth, MSA share and backlog, not premium margins.

name: Centuri Holdings (ex-Southwest Gas utility services)
year: Utility services arm of Southwest Gas; IPO 2024; full separation 2025
acquisitions: Built by acquisition (e.g., Linetec, Riggs Distler per company history; not re-verified this run)
evidence: Record revenue +13%, adj. EBITDA $249.0M, base GM up to 8.0% from 6.9%, net leverage down to 2.5x from 3.6x, 2026 guide $280-310M adj. EBITDA
lesson: The closest public analogue to a gas+electric utility MRO platform: recurring MSA revenue gives durability but only high-single-digit EBITDA margins, and margin gains came from execution and deleveraging, not scale alone.

name: Artera Services (formerly PowerTeam Services)
sponsor: Private; sponsor reported as Kohlberg & Co. (not confirmed this run)
acquisitions: Miller Pipeline + Minnesota Limited from CenterPoint for $850M (closed Apr 2020; ~4,900 employees combined, 35 states)
evidence: Moody's CFR cut to Caa1 (Aug 2022: weak earnings, high leverage, liquidity risk); BDC lenders marked first-lien loans down ~20% (Q2 2022); S&P cut to CCC+ with negative outlook (Dec 2025)
lesson: The most direct precedent for a gas-first MRO roll-up: a big leveraged platform deal on utility MSA work with thin margins left little cushion. Leverage discipline matters more than scale.

name: Pike Corporation
sponsor: TPG Rise Climate + La Caisse (since Dec 2025); previously Lindsay Goldberg
year: Public 2005 (S-1), later private; Lindsay Goldberg 50.1% in 2020
evidence: Majority stake sold to TPG and La Caisse in Dec 2025; Octus estimated valuation above $5B (unconfirmed); ~12,000 employees, 400+ customers
lesson: T&D maintenance and storm-restoration scale with deep IOU relationships commands strong sponsor demand, but that also sets high entry prices for newcomers.

name: Shermco Industries
acquisitions: Tuck-ins of regional NETA firms: Southwest Energy Systems (2019), Power Test (2024), Power Products & Solutions, R3L Engineering (2025), Eastern High Voltage (2025), Power Quality Engineering (2026), NextGen Technologies
evidence: Blackstone acquisition valued at ~$1.6B (Oct 2025); ~40 service centers, 600+ NETA technicians
lesson: A single technically gated niche (NETA-accredited testing) is a repeatable roll-up with a premium exit. Growth leaned on data-center and C&I demand, not only utilities.

name: Osmose Utilities Services
acquisitions: McLean Engineering (pole-attachment/electrical engineering) after EQT deal; others not quantified
evidence: Sponsor-to-sponsor sale to EQT Infrastructure in Jan 2019 (terms undisclosed); continued add-ons; no distress found (weak evidence)
lesson: Inspection and restoration of utility poles is a durable, recurring niche attractive to infrastructure-style capital with long hold periods.

name: USIC
sponsor: Partners Group (from Leonard Green, 2017; current ownership not re-confirmed)
acquisitions: Ongoing tuck-ins, e.g., Heath Consultants' gas locating business (2025), Premier Utility Services, Utility Resource Group
evidence: Three successive sponsor owners; still consolidating in 2025. Credit and financial performance not verified this run
lesson: Recurring 811 locating, driven by regulatory mandate, is a proven multi-sponsor roll-up across all utility types. It is the one example of real cross-utility utilization, but it is a single service line.

name: Badger Infrastructure Solutions
acquisitions: Primarily organic fleet growth; record fleet build planned for 2026
evidence: Revenue +12%, adj. EBITDA +13% to $198.2M, revenue per truck per month up to $41,672
lesson: An equipment-centric specialty service (hydrovac), with in-house manufacturing of its fleet, earns 2-3x the margins of general utility contracting. It shows the value of owning and building the equipment base within one niche.

name: Davey Tree Expert Company
evidence: Record revenue +5.8%, but net income fell 48.6% to $33.3M on insurance, labor, vehicle and interest costs
lesson: Utility vegetation management is the purest recurring utility MRO, but labor-heavy work with low switching costs earns thin margins, and insurance and labor inflation hit hard.

name: Mistras Group
acquisitions: Historically acquisitive inspection/NDE consolidator (count not verified this run)
evidence: Revenue roughly flat; adj. EBITDA +10.5% to $91.1M; $12.7M reorganization costs
lesson: Inspection roll-ups plateau without organic growth. Margin gains come from restructuring and mix, not volume.

name: Team Inc
acquisitions: History of large acquisitions (not re-verified this run)
evidence: Q1 2025 net loss $29.7M incl. $11.9M debt-extinguishment loss; March 2025 refinancing to 2030; cost program of at least $10M
lesson: A debt-funded inspection/mechanical-services roll-up serving industrial and power customers can stay at low-single-digit margins for years. Callout-driven work is not truly recurring.

name: Williams Industrial Services Group
acquisitions: Assets sold to EnergySolutions for $60M in Ch. 11 (2023)
evidence: Chapter 11 July 2023; $19.5M DIP; going-concern warning; cause: loss of large customer contracts in 2022 and losses in water operations
lesson: Plant-maintenance MRO with concentrated customers, plus diversification into fixed-price water work, was fatal. These are the usual risks to screen out.

name: Orbital Infrastructure Group
acquisitions: Built via acquisitions incl. Front Line Power Construction and Gibson Technical Services (both went to lenders in 363 sale)
evidence: Chapter 11 Aug 2023 with $100-500M liabilities; liquidation plan approved Nov 2023
lesson: A leveraged multi-segment 'diversified infrastructure services' roll-up mixing T&D, telecom and renewables construction collapsed. Diversification did not deliver synergies.

name: Charge Enterprises
evidence: Prepackaged Chapter 11 Mar 2024 handing control to lender Arena; $114.3M assets / $48.7M liabilities
lesson: A small-cap infrastructure-services roll-up with weak treasury and governance controls failed despite secular-growth end markets.

name: Infrastructure and Energy Alternatives (IEA)
sponsor: Formerly NASDAQ: IEA; acquired by MasTec (NYSE: MTZ)
acquisitions: Acquired by MasTec Oct 2022 at ~$1.1B EV ($10.50 cash + 0.0483 MTZ per share)
lesson: Construction-led renewables roll-ups end up as tuck-ins for the large strategics rather than standalone compounders.

name: Aegion / Azuria Water Solutions (Insituform)
acquisitions: Brands include Insituform, Corrpro, Underground Solutions, MTC
evidence: Taken private at $963M announced ($30/sh at close, May 2021); rebranded Azuria in 2024 with a water focus
lesson: The public multi-segment pipe-rehab/corrosion/energy-services roll-up underperformed and was refocused on water rehab under private ownership. Focus beat breadth.

name: Vortex Companies
acquisitions: ~12 total per Mergr (weak), incl. Tri-State Utilities and Pipe Vision (from ORIX's National Underground Group), Lining Division (UK)
evidence: Second-sponsor ownership with an active add-on cadence; reported entry ~$160M (unconfirmed)
lesson: Trenchless water/sewer rehabilitation is an active, competitive roll-up lane that a new water platform would bid against.

name: Utility Service Co (USG Water Solutions)
sponsor: Acquired by Suez/United Water 2008 (current owner not verified)
evidence: Strategic acquisition by a water utility operator in 2008
lesson: Long-term water-tank maintenance contracts with municipalities are recurring MRO that strategics will buy. It is a template for a water maintenance unit.
